# M2-S7: eject rewrites value-used unions to methods-only interfaces.
# The m module uses union values, an exhaustive type switch, assertions,
# and a switch expression; the ejected tree builds with plain go and
# prints the same output. The mdual module uses one union as a
# constraint and as a value, so logos eject fails with the pinned text
# while the native run still works.

env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

cd m
logos run .
stdout '^A:1$'
stdout '^got A$'
stdout '^got B$'
stdout '^pick A$'
stdout '^assert A: 1$'
stdout '^member$'
stdout '^non-member$'
cp stdout $WORK/eject-stdout.txt

logos eject -o out
exists out/main.go
exists out/go.mod
grep 'loGo/s union: A \| B' out/main.go
cd out
go build ./...
go run .
cmp stdout $WORK/eject-stdout.txt
cd ..
cd out
go vet ./...
exec $GOROOT/bin/gofmt -l .
! stdout .
cd ..
cd ..

# A dual-use union is valid native code but has no Go form.
cd mdual
logos run .
stdout '^B$'
stdout '^A$'
! logos eject -o out
stderr 'logos eject: union D is used as a type constraint and as a value type; Go cannot express both'

-- m/go.mod --
module example.com/ejectunion

go 1.27

-- m/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("A:%d", a.X)
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B:" + b.Y
}

// U is a closed union used as a value type.
type U interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func Who(x U) string {
	return x.M()
}

func Pick(n int) U {
	if n == 0 {
		return A{X: 1}
	}
	return B{Y: "two"}
}

func Describe(u U) string {
	switch u.(type) {
	case A:
		return "got A"
	case B:
		return "got B"
	case nil:
		return "got nil"
	}
	return "unreachable"
}

func Choose(u U) string {
	return switch u.(type) {
	case A => "pick A"
	case B => "pick B"
	case nil => "pick nil"
	}
}

func Check(v any) string {
	if _, ok := v.(U); ok {
		return "member"
	}
	return "non-member"
}

// C sits outside the member set of U. It deliberately implements no
// methods: a methods-only interface (which is what eject writes for U)
// would accept any non-member that implements M, so the shared output
// below only asserts membership behavior that native and ejected code
// agree on.
type C struct {
	Z int
}

func main() {
	u := Pick(0)
	fmt.Println(Who(u))
	fmt.Println(Describe(u))
	fmt.Println(Describe(B{Y: "x"}))
	fmt.Println(Choose(u))
	if a, ok := u.(A); ok {
		fmt.Println("assert A:", a.X)
	}
	fmt.Println(Check(A{X: 2}))
	fmt.Println(Check(C{}))
}

-- mdual/go.mod --
module example.com/dualunion

go 1.27

-- mdual/main.lgo --
package main

import "fmt"

type A struct {
	X int
}

func (a A) M() string {
	return "A"
}

type B struct {
	Y string
}

func (b B) M() string {
	return "B"
}

// D is used as a constraint and as a value: it has no Go form.
type D interface {
	A | B
	M() string
}

func First[T D](x T) T {
	return x
}

var u D = A{X: 3}

func main() {
	fmt.Println(First(B{Y: "z"}).M())
	fmt.Println(u.M())
}
